key_insight: A short, brain-inspired warm-up training phase with random noise applied after initialization fixes initialization-induced overconfidence in deep nets, yielding substantially better probability calibration and recognition of unknown inputs.
problem_solved: Deep neural networks are often overconfident due to standard parameter initialization, which harms uncertainty estimates and detection of out-of-distribution/unknown inputs.
method: Introduce a brief warm-up stage immediately after initialization where the network is trained only on random noise (no labels).
Proceed with standard supervised training after warm-up; the noise phase reshapes early representations and reduces unwarranted confidence.
Evaluate improvements using calibration metrics (ECE/reliability diagrams) and meta-cognitive OOD/unknown recognition benchmarks.
impact: This is a simple, low-cost modification to training that improves reliability and trustworthiness of model probabilities and OOD detection—useful for safety-critical and uncertainty-sensitive ML deployments.
visual_elements: Training timeline diagram: initialization → short noise warm-up (highlighted) → standard training
Before/after reliability diagrams or calibration curves (showing overconfidence reduction)
Bar chart comparing calibration error and OOD detection metrics with vs. without warm-up
Illustrative icon set: neuron/init icon, noise symbol, and a confidence gauge to convey 'less overconfident'
paper_title: Brain-inspired warm-up training with random noise for uncertainty calibration
